# Research Note: Costco Wholesale Corporation (COST)
**Date: May 2026**

---

## Snapshot

**Company:** Costco Wholesale Corporation  
**Ticker:** COST (NASDAQ)  
**Current Price:** $1,011.70 USD  
**Market Capitalization:** $448.8 billion [Source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance]  
**P/E Ratio (TTM):** 52.64 [Source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance]  
**52-Week Range:** $844.06 - $1,067.08 [Source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance]  
**1-Month Price Change:** -0.18% [Source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance]  
**Sector:** Consumer Defensive | **Industry:** Discount Stores [Source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance]

**Revenue (TTM):** $286.3 billion [Source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance]  
**Warehouse Count:** 924 warehouses globally (634 US & Puerto Rico, 114 Canada, 176 other international) [Source: https://investor.costco.com/news/news-details/2026/Costco-Wholesale-Corporation-Reports-Second-Quarter-and-Year-to-Date-Operating-Results-for-Fiscal-2026-and-February-Sales-Results/default.aspx]

**Macro Context:**  
Federal Funds Rate at 3.64% (falling trend), unemployment at 4.3% (rising trend), 10Y-2Y Treasury spread at 0.51 bps (falling but positive), S&P 500 at 7,230 (rising trend). The falling rate environment with positive yield curve supports consumer discretionary spending, though rising unemployment presents headwinds. [Source: FRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis)]

---

## Bull Case

1. **Exceptional Comparable Sales Momentum Across All Geographies**  
   For Q2 FY2026 (12 weeks ended February 15, 2026), total company comparable sales increased 7.4%, or 6.7% excluding gasoline and FX impacts. March 2026 comparable sales accelerated to 9.4% despite one fewer shopping day due to Easter timing. U.S. comps grew 8.7%, Canada 10.7%, and Other International 11.9% in March. [Source: https://investor.costco.com/news/news-details/2026/Costco-Wholesale-Corporation-Reports-March-Sales-Results/default.aspx and https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2897372/costcos-comparable-sales-stay-resilient-despite-calendar-headwind]

2. **Membership Fee Revenue Surging Post-September 2024 Increase**  
   Membership fee revenue reached $1.36 billion in Q2 FY2026, up 13.6% year-over-year. For the first 24 weeks of FY2026, membership fees totaled $2.68 billion versus $2.36 billion prior year. The September 2024 fee increase ($5 for Gold Star, $10 for Executive) is flowing directly to the bottom line at near-100% margins, with each $5 increase on 81.4M members generating approximately $407M in additional annual income. [Source: https://www.mexc.com/news/1067968 and https://investor.costco.com/news/news-details/2026/Costco-Wholesale-Corporation-Reports-Second-Quarter-and-Year-to-Date-Operating-Results-for-Fiscal-2026-and-February-Sales-Results/default.aspx]

3. **Digital Commerce Explosive Growth**  
   Digitally-enabled comparable sales surged 22.6% in Q2 FY2026 and 21.8% in February, significantly outpacing physical warehouse growth. Year-to-date digital comps are up 21.6%, demonstrating successful omnichannel execution without cannibalizing core warehouse traffic. [Source: https://investor.costco.com/news/news-details/2026/Costco-Wholesale-Corporation-Reports-Second-Quarter-and-Year-to-Date-Operating-Results-for-Fiscal-2026-and-February-Sales-Results/default.aspx]

4. **Traffic-Driven Growth Model Demonstrates Pricing Power**  
   Traffic growth, not just ticket size, remains the primary driver of comparable sales performance. This indicates strong member engagement and the ability to attract new customers despite the 2024 membership fee increase, validating the strength of Costco's value proposition. [Source: https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2888678/costcos-comparable-sales-stay-strong-is-traffic-driving-growth]

5. **Strong Earnings Growth with Operating Leverage**  
   Q2 FY2026 net income reached $2.04 billion ($4.58 diluted EPS) versus $1.79 billion ($4.02 diluted EPS) prior year, representing 13.9% earnings growth. Operating margin expanded as merchandise costs as a percentage of sales improved. Year-to-date net income of $4.04 billion ($9.08 EPS) compares to $3.59 billion ($8.06 EPS) last year, up 12.7%. [Source: https://investor.costco.com/news/news-details/2026/Costco-Wholesale-Corporation-Reports-Second-Quarter-and-Year-to-Date-Operating-Results-for-Fiscal-2026-and-February-Sales-Results/default.aspx]

---

## Bear Case

1. **Extremely Elevated Valuation Multiple at Historic Highs**  
   At a P/E ratio of 52.64 (TTM) and forward P/E near 50, COST trades 39% above its 10-year median P/E of 37.26. This valuation embeds expectations for flawless execution and leaves minimal room for disappointment. Multiple compression risk is substantial—a reversion to historical averages would erase years of earnings growth even with strong operational performance. [Source: https://www.gurufocus.com/term/pettm/%20COST and https://www.tikr.com/blog/costco-stock-is-up-17-in-2026-while-the-market-falls-is-it-still-worth-buying-at-1000]

2. **Margin Pressure from Low Single-Digit Inflation Environment**  
   Management noted low single-digit inflation in non-foods during Q2 2026 earnings commentary, with gas prices down low-to-mid single digits year-over-year. In a deflationary or very low inflation environment, Costco's razor-thin operating margin of 3.77% faces compression risk as the company cannot easily offset cost pressures through price increases without violating its value proposition. [Source: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/03/05/costco-cost-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/ and Financial Modeling Prep]

3. **Rising Unemployment Threatens Consumer Spending**  
   The unemployment rate has risen to 4.3% with an upward trend. As unemployment climbs, discretionary spending typically contracts, and even value retailers face traffic headwinds. While Costco may gain market share from premium competitors during economic stress, absolute transaction volumes could decline. [Source: FRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis)]

4. **Limited Membership Fee Increase Runway Until 2027-2028**  
   With the last fee increase implemented in September 2024, historical patterns suggest the next increase won't occur until 2027-2028 (fees previously increased every 5-7 years). This removes a significant near-term catalyst and means membership revenue growth will depend primarily on new member additions rather than per-member rate increases. [Source: https://www.mexc.com/news/1067968 and https://20somethingfinance.com/costco-membership-fees]

5. **High Debt-to-Equity Relative to Historical Conservative Balance Sheet**  
   While the debt-to-equity ratio of 0.28 appears moderate, it represents elevated leverage for a traditionally conservative balance sheet company. With $5.7 billion in long-term debt and rising interest expenses in a higher-for-longer rate environment, interest coverage could tighten if operating performance falters. [Source: Financial Modeling Prep and https://investor.costco.com/news/news-details/2026/Costco-Wholesale-Corporation-Reports-Second-Quarter-and-Year-to-Date-Operating-Results-for-Fiscal-2026-and-February-Sales-Results/default.aspx]

## Recent Catalysts

1. **Q2 FY2026 Earnings Beat (March 5, 2026)**  
   Costco reported Q2 net sales of $68.24 billion (+9.1% YoY) and EPS of $4.58 (vs. $4.02 prior year), exceeding analyst expectations. Comparable sales of 7.4% total company (6.7% adjusted) demonstrated continued momentum. [Source: https://investor.costco.com/news/news-details/2026/Costco-Wholesale-Corporation-Reports-Second-Quarter-and-Year-to-Date-Operating-Results-for-Fiscal-2026-and-February-Sales-Results/default.aspx]

2. **March 2026 Sales Report Shows Accelerating Comps (April 8, 2026)**  
   March comparable sales of 9.4% exceeded expectations despite one fewer shopping day due to Easter calendar shift. Net sales reached $28.41 billion for the five-week period, up 11.3% YoY. This marked acceleration from February's 7.9% comp and January's 7.1% comp. [Source: https://investor.costco.com/news/news-details/2026/Costco-Wholesale-Corporation-Reports-March-Sales-Results/default.aspx]

3. **Most Recent 8-K Filing (April 15, 2026)**  
   Costco filed an 8-K on April 15, 2026, likely containing monthly sales updates or material event disclosure. [Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/909832/000090983226000041/cost-20260415.htm]

4. **Analyst Price Target Increases**  
   Mizuho and other brokers raised 12-month price targets to the low-to-mid-$1,000s range in February 2026 based on strong membership income growth and consistent comparable sales performance. Consensus targets cluster around current price levels. [Source: https://capital.com/en-int/maket-updates/costco-stock-forecast-17-02-2026]

## Risks

**Company-Specific Risks:**

1. **Valuation Compression Risk:** At 52x P/E, any earnings miss or guidance reduction could trigger significant multiple contraction. The stock trades at a 39% premium to its 10-year median valuation, leaving limited downside protection. [Source: https://www.gurufocus.com/term/pettm/%20COST]

2. **Margin Compression in Low-Inflation Environment:** With operating margins of only 3.77% and net margins of 2.94%, Costco has minimal buffer to absorb cost pressures. Low single-digit inflation limits pricing power while wage pressures and rising healthcare costs persist. [Source: Financial Modeling Prep]

3. **Membership Renewal Rate Deterioration Risk:** Any decline in the renewal rate below 89.5% would signal weakening value proposition and threaten the predictable revenue stream that justifies premium valuation. Digital membership additions may have lower renewal rates than traditional warehouse-acquired members. [Source: https://www.tikr.com/blog/costco-stock-is-up-17-in-2026-while-the-market-falls-is-it-still-worth-buying-at-1000]

4. **International Expansion Execution Risk:** While Other International markets show strongest comp growth (11.9% in March), operating in 14+ countries exposes Costco to currency volatility, regulatory differences, and localization challenges. [Source: https://investor.costco.com/news/news-details/2026/Costco-Wholesale-Corporation-Reports-March-Sales-Results/default.aspx]

**Macro Risks:**

1. **Rising Unemployment:** The 4.3% unemployment rate with upward trend threatens consumer spending capacity, particularly for discretionary categories beyond grocery staples. [Source: FRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis)]

2. **Falling Federal Funds Rate Signals Economic Weakness:** While lower rates typically benefit consumers, the falling trend from higher levels suggests the Fed is responding to economic softness, which could impact warehouse traffic and average ticket. [Source: FRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis)]

3. **Compressed Yield Curve (Falling Spread):** The 10Y-2Y spread at 0.51 bps is falling, historically a recessionary signal when it inverts or remains narrow. [Source: FRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis)]

---

## What to Watch Next

1. **Q3 FY2026 Earnings Report (May 28, 2026 After Market Close)**  
   Next earnings date confirmed for late May 2026. Consensus EPS estimate is $5.00, with revenue estimated at $70.41 billion. Key metrics to monitor: membership renewal rates (must hold above 89.5%), digitally-enabled comp sales momentum (sustaining 20%+ growth), and any commentary on traffic versus ticket mix. [Source: https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/COST/analyst-ratings and Financial Modeling Prep]

2. **April and May Monthly Sales Releases**  
   Costco announces monthly sales results approximately 5 weeks after period end. Watch for sustained 8-10% comparable sales growth and any deceleration that might signal consumer spending weakness. Geographic mix trends (U.S. versus international) will indicate where growth is concentrating. [Source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance]

3. **Membership Renewal Rate Disclosure**  
   Management typically discusses renewal rates quarterly. Any decline below the mid-to-high 80s percentage range would be a significant red flag given the premium valuation. Specific disclosure of digital-acquired member renewal rates versus warehouse-acquired members would provide transparency on channel quality. [Source: https://www.tikr.com/blog/costco-stock-is-up-17-in-2026-while-the-market-falls-is-it-still-worth-buying-at-1000]

**Analyst Perspective:**  
Costco continues to execute at an elite level with accelerating comparable sales, robust digital growth, and membership fee tailwinds from the 2024 increase. However, the stock's 52x P/E ratio prices in perfection and offers minimal margin of safety. The bull case hinges on sustained high-single-digit comp growth and stable renewal rates; the bear case revolves around valuation compression and macro headwinds. Current valuation appears appropriate only for investors with high conviction in Costco's defensive qualities during potential economic softness and a multi-year holding period to grow into the multiple.
